// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["b88c5744975d2abb447aecc6c090fee9f8580413f4612eecdc6ed1973e8a1739", "ed5ae7f36453c5a23e9868a5729d67e0549a11f6dea54f5f52d654a8f51d4902", "841c9297cb8a2e0ff89433d13c05bfc760eb2e98e251cb8fa785d2ad7cbac05f", "ece7c48eb411b24f26762ede83badb4a644c41d5777129381ac2541804d64fc2", "421ce2d2f49c23bbe9f60ef3b9cd38d7eb912ce02e56a61837656210069bd9e2", "121c2dc793b3873f75a29ec02241f94136de19c049382a50a50d0d5b99507073", "2415db5081cec9bfd14ad6da1a66169fd96f13a49010c319a73d1ed6fafd4efa", "d9917ade3b4c125a95b5d3e6343cde26145dfbf569bd7e2a843fd0c6fc8ddc28", "4cf6893756f441522b94b36f10e5de0e47aeed4743f95c51650746d1ecf97e3d", "8b89d6c9152d3aab97aadd515ecb69ca72654db2f25425759ba4b646853d737d", "90ce4ff9da23ac150da0a8e17930cab1e369aa349fdc1b65691b70369145664a"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant · Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change · LSASS process access / dump (credential theft)
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |
    Replace `__IP_LIST__` / `__DOMAIN_LIST__` placeholders with
    article-specific destinations. For dynamic IOC management, use a
    watchlist or external feed.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/tactics/TA0011/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.command-and-control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_ip:
        DestinationIp:
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__IP_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    selection_domain:
        DestinationHostname:
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_1__'
            - '__DOMAIN_PLACEHOLDER_2__'
    condition: selection_ip or selection_domain
falsepositives:
    - None on a true-positive IOC match
level: critical
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("176.120.22.127")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("176.120.22.127")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Vulnerabilities
    where Vulnerabilities.signature IN ("CVE-2024-55591", "CVE-2025-32433", "CVE-2025-33073", "CVE-2026-11645", "CVE-2026-20230", "CVE-2026-23479")
    by Vulnerabilities.dest, Vulnerabilities.signature, Vulnerabilities.severity, Vulnerabilities.cve
| `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)`
| sort - severity

SecurityEvent

| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 1m)
| where files > 200    // P99 of legit bulk-tooling per-minute rename volume
| order by files desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web

| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60

Miasma 'Phantom Gyp' — 157-byte binding.gyp drop in node_modules AIInstallation High
Detects the Miasma worm's Phantom Gyp technique: a tiny binding.gyp file (~157 bytes) planted inside a node_modules subtree to trigger code execution via npm's native-build step, bypassing preinstall/postinstall script gating. Legitimate node-gyp manifests are typically far larger than 220 bytes. Rationale: Article states Miasma ships a 157-byte binding.gyp as its execution vector ('Phantom Gyp'). Filtering by FileName + node_modules path + small size targets this specific artifact while excluding legitimate native-module builds whose binding.gyp files declare full target/source/include trees (typically >1KB).
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate tiny binding.gyp shims in obscure community packages
  • Test fixtures in node-gyp's own test suite
  • Developer hand-creating a minimal binding.gyp during native-addon scaffolding
  • Old cached binding.gyp from a node_modules directory pre-dating native code
  • Documentation/tutorial scaffolding under /sample-projects/
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp configure", "node-gyp rebuild", "npm test")) | where not(FolderPath has_any ("\\node-gyp\\test\\", "\\node_modules\\sharp\\", "\\node_modules\\sqlite3\\", "\\node_modules\\node-sass\\"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Pull the binding.gyp content via DeviceFileEvents.SHA256 → VirusTotal and read first 200 bytes; legitimate manifests start with `{ "targets": [...] }`, Miasma's variants contain `child_process`/`exec`/`require('http')` strings. Pivot DeviceProcessEvents to find the npm install ancestor and identify the parent package name. Step 2 — contain: Isolate the host via Defender Live Response; revoke and rotate the developer's npm publish token at registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/tokens; quarantine the implicated package from internal mirrors. Step 3 — hunt: Sweep the fleet for the same SHA256 and for outbound HTTP to any URL referenced in the binding.gyp body; correlate against the developer's recent `npm publish` activity to map worm spread radius.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where FileSize between (50 .. 220)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "binding.gyp"
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where TargetFileSize between (50 .. 220)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Auto-execute editor/AI-tool config file dropped in repository AIInstallation High
Detects file creation of the specific editor and AI-coding-assistant integration files Miasma/Hades planted to obtain on-project-open code execution: .vscode/tasks.json, .vscode/setup.mjs, .claude/setup.mjs, .claude/settings.json, .cursor/rules/setup.mdc, .gemini/settings.json, .github/setup.js. Highest signal when written by a package manager (node/npm/pip/python) rather than the editor itself. Rationale: Article's IOC table enumerates exactly these seven file paths and their auto-execute triggers (SessionStart hook, folderOpen task, custom rules load, settings injection). Constraining the parent to a package manager filters out the legitimate case where the editor itself writes these files via user action.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1547.013 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legit npm packages whose postinstall scaffolds VS Code launch tasks (e.g. ts-node create-app templates)
  • Python packages with pyproject.toml scaffolding tooling that writes .vscode settings
  • Yarn berry zero-installs writing PnP-related .vscode files
  • Internal developer tooling that ships standard project templates including .vscode/tasks.json
  • Cookiecutter / yeoman generators executed via node.exe parent
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("create-react-app", "create-next-app", "cookiecutter", "yo ", "yeoman", "create-vite"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Read the dropped file's contents (DeviceFileEvents.SHA256 → file capture); legit tasks.json declares lint/build tasks, Miasma variants contain `runOn: folderOpen` plus a child `command` that downloads a payload. Pivot to DeviceProcessEvents to find the npm/pip install ancestor and identify the source package. Step 2 — contain: Revoke the developer's npm/PyPI publishing tokens; remove the file before the developer next opens the project; quarantine the source package in the internal mirror. Step 3 — hunt: Across all dev machines, list every recent write to any of the seven paths regardless of parent; cross-reference with git history of the affected repos to determine whether the file was also committed and pushed to remote (indicating GitHub-org spread, as the article notes happened to 73 Azure repos).
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath contains ".vscode" and FileName in~ ("tasks.json", "setup.mjs"))
     or (FolderPath contains ".claude" and FileName in~ ("setup.mjs", "settings.json"))
     or (FolderPath contains ".cursor" and FileName =~ "setup.mdc")
     or (FolderPath contains ".gemini" and FileName =~ "settings.json")
     or (FolderPath contains ".github" and FileName =~ "setup.js")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "npm.exe", "yarn.exe", "pnpm.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "pip.exe", "pip3.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, FileSize, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (TargetFilePath contains ".vscode" and TargetFileName in~ ("tasks.json", "setup.mjs"))
     or (TargetFilePath contains ".claude" and TargetFileName in~ ("setup.mjs", "settings.json"))
     or (TargetFilePath contains ".cursor" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.mdc")
     or (TargetFilePath contains ".gemini" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json")
     or (TargetFilePath contains ".github" and TargetFileName =~ "setup.js")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node.exe", "npm.exe", "yarn.exe", "pnpm.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "pip.exe", "pip3.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSize, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

VS Code / Cursor / Claude Code spawning script interpreter on project open AIInstallation High
Detects developer IDEs and AI coding assistants (code.exe, cursor.exe, claude.exe, gemini.exe) spawning script interpreters (node.exe, python.exe, bun.exe, pwsh.exe) where the child command line references the article's auto-execute payload paths (setup.mjs, setup.mdc, tasks.json) or downloads Bun. This is the on-open execution moment for both Miasma and Hades. Rationale: Article specifies that opening a project in VS Code/Cursor/Claude Code triggers the payload via .vscode/tasks.json runOn:folderOpen, .claude/setup.mjs SessionStart hook, and Cursor custom rules load. The parent==editor + child==interpreter + cmdline-references-payload-path triad is the only place this attack surfaces in process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • VS Code task runner legitimately executing .vscode/tasks.json (build, lint, test tasks)
  • Claude Code session-start hook running a legit project setup.mjs
  • Cursor's own rule loader processing setup.mdc on first project open
  • Python virtualenv activation script invoked by integrated terminal
  • node.exe spawned by VS Code's TypeScript language server with project paths in argv
Suppression filter
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("tsc.js", "eslint", "vitest", "jest", "prettier", "webpack")) | where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--task=build")
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Inspect the ProcessCommandLine for outbound URLs, eval(), atob(), or child_process — legit task runners pass declarative args, malicious chains invoke download-and-exec primitives. Pull DeviceFileEvents for the setup.mjs/tasks.json SHA256 and confirm whether content matches the article's pattern. Step 2 — contain: Kill the orphan child (node/python/bun) before it completes credential harvest; isolate host; revoke developer's npm/PyPI publishing tokens immediately. Step 3 — hunt: For 24h around the alert, surface DeviceNetworkEvents from the child process to identify the C2 / Bun-runtime download endpoint; pivot DeviceFileEvents on the editor's account for any other auto-execute config files dropped recently across all repos under %USERPROFILE%\\source\\ or similar dev-roots.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe", "cursor.exe", "claude.exe", "gemini.exe", "windsurf.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("node.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "bun.exe", "wsl.exe", "bash.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "setup.js", "setup.mdc", "tasks.json", ".claude", ".cursor", ".vscode", ".gemini", "bun.sh", "oven-sh/bun", "DownloadString", "child_process")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\code.exe", "\\cursor.exe", "\\claude.exe", "\\gemini.exe", "\\windsurf.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\python.exe", "\\python3.exe", "\\pwsh.exe", "\\powershell.exe", "\\cmd.exe", "\\bun.exe", "\\wsl.exe", "\\bash.exe")
| where CommandLine has_any ("setup.mjs", "setup.js", "setup.mdc", "tasks.json", ".claude", ".cursor", ".vscode", ".gemini", "bun.sh", "oven-sh/bun", "DownloadString", "child_process")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Hades — python.exe child process downloads standalone Bun runtime on import AICommand & Control High
Detects Hades' PyPI execution chain: an obfuscated __init__.py import hook spawns a download of the standalone Bun runtime (bun.exe or the bun-windows/linux archive from bun.sh / github.com/oven-sh/bun) to execute the JavaScript payload. Python parent + Bun child or curl/PowerShell child fetching Bun is highly anomalous outside this campaign. Rationale: Article: 'the hook downloads a standalone Bun runtime and runs a JavaScript payload'. Python as a parent spawning a Bun fetch is the specific TTP — bun.sh / oven-sh/bun host the canonical download URLs, and bun.exe is the resulting runtime binary. Bun is not in the standard Python toolchain.
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.006 T1059.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually installing Bun via a pip helper script
  • ML/data-science project using a Bun-based JS bridge
  • CI image build pulling Bun for a polyglot project
  • Bun's own Python SDK installer (if/when it exists)
  • System administrator scripts that benchmark JS runtimes
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("install-bun", "setup-bun", "pip install bun"))
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Identify the Python parent's source — DeviceProcessEvents InitiatingProcessCommandLine usually carries `python -c "import X"` or `python -m X` indicating the package; cross-check against ensmallen and the ~24 ML/bioinformatics packages the article names. Step 2 — contain: Isolate host; kill bun.exe; uninstall the suspect PyPI package globally and from the user's venv; revoke PyPI publishing token via pypi.org account settings. Step 3 — hunt: Sweep fleet for python.exe→bun.exe parentage in last 30d; sweep DeviceNetworkEvents for traffic to bun.sh from python.exe across all hosts; pull SHA256 of the bun.exe binary written to disk and compare against the article's IOC hashes.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python.exe", "python3.exe", "pythonw.exe")
| where (FileName in~ ("curl.exe", "powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", "cmd.exe", "wget.exe")
         and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh", "oven-sh/bun", "bun-windows", "bun-linux", "bun-darwin"))
   or FileName =~ "bun.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\python.exe", "\\python3.exe", "\\pythonw.exe")
| where (NewProcessName has_any ("\\curl.exe", "\\powershell.exe", "\\pwsh.exe", "\\cmd.exe", "\\wget.exe")
         and CommandLine has_any ("bun.sh", "oven-sh/bun", "bun-windows", "bun-linux", "bun-darwin"))
   or NewProcessName endswith "\\bun.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Hades - Python Import Hook Downloads Standalone Bun Runtime

Miasma/Hades worm credential theft — npm/PyPI publishing token access AIActions on Objectives High
Detects Miasma/Hades' worm-propagation step: post-execution Bun/Node/Python child of a developer IDE reading or referencing npm (.npmrc, NPM_TOKEN, _authToken) or PyPI (.pypirc, PYPI_TOKEN, __token__) publishing credentials. The article explicitly states the worm searches for npm/PyPI publishing tokens then republishes infected versions. Rationale: Article: 'it searches for npm and PyPI publishing tokens, then republishes infected versions'. The credential-theft step is what turns each victim into a spreader. Detecting node/bun/python (parent = IDE) touching .npmrc / .pypirc / token env-vars surfaces this without depending on file-read telemetry (which Defender doesn't carry for read-only access).
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1528 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually running `npm publish` or `twine upload` from VS Code integrated terminal
  • CI/CD scripts running under devcontainer touching .npmrc
  • Setup scripts in legitimate packages that reference NPM_TOKEN env var
  • Yarn/pnpm publish workflows
  • Jenkins build agent on a developer's box performing release
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm whoami", "npm view", "npm config get")) | where not(ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)^.*npm\s+(version|whoami|view|outdated|ls)\b.*$")
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Confirm whether the developer performed a publish action in the matching window via their personal log or git history (look for `npm version` / `twine` immediately preceding). If no human action, this is the worm. Step 2 — contain: Immediately revoke ALL active npm publish tokens for the account at npmjs.com/settings/tokens and PyPI tokens at pypi.org/manage/account/token/; rotate any CI tokens; force-revoke ssh keys; isolate the host. Step 3 — hunt: List the packages the affected token CAN publish (npm whoami + npm access ls-packages) and treat each as suspect — pull the last 72h of versions from npmjs.com/PyPI registry and diff against legitimate maintainer history. Notify package consumers of potential downstream compromise.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".npmrc", ".pypirc", "_authToken", "NPM_TOKEN", "PYPI_TOKEN", "NPM_AUTH_TOKEN", "registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/tokens", "username = __token__", "twine upload", "npm publish", "__token__")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe", "bun.exe", "python.exe", "python3.exe", "pwsh.exe", "powershell.exe", "cmd.exe", "npm.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe", "cursor.exe", "claude.exe", "gemini.exe", "python.exe", "node.exe", "npm.exe", "bun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          GrandparentImage = InitiatingProcessParentFileName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where CommandLine has_any (".npmrc", ".pypirc", "_authToken", "NPM_TOKEN", "PYPI_TOKEN", "NPM_AUTH_TOKEN", "registry.npmjs.org/-/npm/v1/tokens", "username = __token__", "twine upload", "npm publish", "__token__")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\\code.exe", "\\cursor.exe", "\\claude.exe", "\\gemini.exe", "\\python.exe", "\\node.exe", "\\bun.exe", "\\npm.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\node.exe", "\\bun.exe", "\\python.exe", "\\python3.exe", "\\pwsh.exe", "\\powershell.exe", "\\cmd.exe", "\\npm.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName,
          ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Known Miasma/Hades payload SHA256 hash observed on developer machine AIInstallation Medium
Direct IOC sweep for the five SHA256 hashes attributed to the Miasma/Hades campaign across DeviceProcessEvents, DeviceFileEvents, and DeviceImageLoadEvents. Hash-based detection is exact-match and high-confidence — any hit is a Sev-1 confirmed compromise. Rationale: Article-supplied IOCs: five SHA256 hashes directly attributed to the Miasma/Hades campaign. Exact hash match across process exec, file write, and image-load surfaces the payload regardless of file name, path, or persistence vector — covers both the on-import and on-open execution paths.
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • No legitimate FPs expected for exact SHA256 match
  • Possible benign hit only if a security tool itself stages the IOC for study (e.g. researcher's analysis VM)
  • StepSecurity's own Suspicious Files agent caching the rule's IOC list locally for fingerprinting
  • Threat-intel feed ingestion writing IOC samples to disk for tooling
Response runbook
Step 1 — triage: Confirm event timestamp and DeviceName; pull DeviceProcessEvents+DeviceFileEvents+DeviceNetworkEvents on that DeviceId for ±30 minutes around the hash sighting to reconstruct full kill chain. Step 2 — contain: Hard-isolate host via Defender Live Response (`Isolate-Machine`); revoke all developer credentials (npm, PyPI, GitHub PAT, SSH, AAD); kill running processes matching the SHA256. Step 3 — hunt: Push the five hashes to all EDR consoles (Defender, CrowdStrike, Cortex) for 90-day retro-hunt; query DeviceFileEvents fleet-wide for the hashes; pull all git push events from the affected developer's machine for the last 7 days to identify which downstream repos may carry the implanted editor/AI-tool config files.
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic([
    "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe",
    "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d",
    "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c",
    "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655",
    "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"
]);
union
  (DeviceProcessEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventType="ProcessExec", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, CmdLine=ProcessCommandLine, AccountName),
  (DeviceFileEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventType="FileWrite", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, CmdLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName),
  (DeviceImageLoadEvents
   | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
   | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
   | project Timestamp, DeviceName, EventType="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
             InitiatingProcessFileName, CmdLine=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName)
| order by Timestamp desc
let MiasmaHashes = dynamic([
    "dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe",
    "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d",
    "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c",
    "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655",
    "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"
]);
union
  (ImProcessCreate
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where SHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType="ProcessExec", TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, SHA256, ActorUsername),
  (ImFileEvent
   | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
   | where TargetFileSHA256 in (MiasmaHashes)
   | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType="FileWrite", TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, SHA256=TargetFileSHA256, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma/Hades Campaign IOC - SHA256 Hash Match

PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command Exploitation High
Encoded or obfuscated PowerShell — common across loaders, recon, and post-exploitation.
ATT&CKT1059.001 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(-enc|encodedcommand|frombase64string|-nop|-w\s+hidden|invoke-expression|iex\s*\(|downloadstring|net\.webclient)"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName,
          CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Obfuscated / Encoded PowerShell Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d08
status: experimental
description: |
    PowerShell launched with -EncodedCommand, base64 strings, hidden
    window, no-profile, bypass policy, IEX / Invoke-Expression / Net
    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1027/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1027
    - attack.execution
    - attack.defense-evasion
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_image:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
    selection_args:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - '-enc '
            - 'EncodedCommand'
            - 'FromBase64String'
            - 'Invoke-Expression'
            - 'IEX('
            - 'DownloadString'
            - 'Net.WebClient'
            - '-w hidden'
            - '-WindowStyle Hidden'
            - '-nop'
            - '-NoProfile'
            - '-ep bypass'
            - '-ExecutionPolicy Bypass'
    condition: selection_image and selection_args
falsepositives:
    - DevOps tooling that legitimately uses encoded command for
      cross-shell escaping
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*-enc *" OR Processes.process="*EncodedCommand*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64String*" OR Processes.process="*-nop*"
        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*IEX(*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*Net.WebClient*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children Exploitation Medium
Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
// Replace `"setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe"` with the vendor binaries observed in the
// article (matching shape with the Defender query).
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\rundll32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\regsvr32.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\bitsadmin.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: Trusted Vendor Binary Launching Unusual Children
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d09
status: experimental
description: |
    A signed vendor binary (in the article's named-vendors list)
    spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Strongest signal when
    paired with a recent CVE / supply-chain advisory naming the same
    vendor.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1195
    - attack.initial-access
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\cmd.exe'
            - '\rundll32.exe'
            - '\regsvr32.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
            - '\wscript.exe'
            - '\cscript.exe'
            - '\wmic.exe'
            - '\bitsadmin.exe'
    selection_parent_vendor:
        ParentImage|contains:
            - '\Program Files\'
            - '\Program Files (x86)\'
    condition: selection_child and selection_parent_vendor
falsepositives:
    - Many — installers and updaters legitimately spawn children. Pin
      the parent path to specific vendor binaries observed in the
      article before alerting.
level: medium
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("setup.exe","installer.exe","update.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","cmd.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or SHA1 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966") or MD5 in~ ("dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["dc48b09b2a5954f7ff79ab8a2fd80202bd3b59c08c7cdbc6025aa923cb4c0efe", "e1342a80d4b5e83d2c7c22e1e0aaa95f2d88e3dbf0d853a4994b180c93a4b17d", "c539766062555d47716f8432e73adbe3a0c0c954a0b6c4005017a668975e275c", "7069e28a5806db4ab0273639667d203f5e31b401d403af7e36d9f360c1f6d655", "b86c5ae9e95bd841a595440faa3eb6317441e746f241ae8fd641ab59ed1d1966"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Malicious npm postinstall payload file drop (Shai-Hulud / Nx s1ngularity) AIInstallation High
Detects the file write of named malicious npm postinstall/preinstall payload files into node_modules during install: telemetry.js (Nx s1ngularity, Aug 2025) and setup_bun.js + bun_environment.js (Shai-Hulud 2.0 + Mini Shai-Hulud, Nov 2025 / May 2026). These exact filenames are the documented payload droppers from the three campaigns the article calls out by name. Rationale: Anchors on the three named-by-campaign filenames in the article body — telemetry.js (Nx s1ngularity), setup_bun.js and bun_environment.js (Shai-Hulud and Mini Shai-Hulud). Microsoft's Shai-Hulud 2.0 guidance and Nx's own post-mortem confirm these are the canonical payload filenames; restricting to node_modules and an npm-family parent process keeps fidelity high. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/12/09/shai-hulud-2-0-guidance-for-detecting-investigating-and-defending-against-the-supply-chain-attack/ • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.007 T1546
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer or red-team importing a captured sample of these files into a sandbox node_modules tree for analysis
  • Security tool (Aikido Safe Chain, Snyk, Socket) quarantining a known-bad package and leaving the original filename in a holding directory under node_modules
  • SOC honeypot npm proxy that mirrors known-bad packages for telemetry
  • Legitimate package coincidentally named telemetry.js inside an unrelated project's node_modules (rare — the Bun ones are unique)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\samples\\","\\sandbox\\","\\quarantine\\","safechain","socket-cli"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full file path and SHA256, compare against the published Shai-Hulud / s1ngularity hash sets, and identify the parent package directory (the package.json one level above the file). Inspect the package's scripts.preinstall / scripts.postinstall fields. 2) Contain: isolate the host (Defender Live Response / CrowdStrike RTR), kill any node.exe / bun.exe still running under that user, and revoke the user's npm publish tokens, GitHub PAT, and AWS keys from the npm cache and `~/.npmrc`. 3) Hunt: pivot on the user's GitHub account for newly-created public repos (s1ngularity-repository*, Shai-Hulud*) and on the host for outbound traffic to bun.sh and api.github.com/user/repos in the 30 minutes after the file write.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("telemetry.js","setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js")
| where FolderPath has "node_modules"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where TargetFileName in~ ("telemetry.js","setup_bun.js","bun_environment.js")
| where TargetFilePath has "node_modules"
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","bun")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects file writes of telemetry.js (Nx s1ngularity), setup_bun.js or bun_environment.js (Shai-Hulud 2.0 / Mini Shai-Hulud) into node_modules during npm install.

TruffleHog execution as descendant of npm/node (Shai-Hulud secret scrape) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the trufflehog secret-scanner binary invoked as a child of npm, node, yarn, pnpm or bun. The article calls out Shai-Hulud explicitly running TruffleHog after install to harvest secrets from the developer machine; downloading and running TruffleHog from an install hook has no legitimate counterpart in normal dependency installation. Rationale: Article explicitly names TruffleHog as the secret-scraping tool Shai-Hulud downloads during install. Gating on an npm-family parent process drops the legitimate CI/SRE use of TruffleHog (which spawns from runner agents, not from `node.exe`). Microsoft, Unit42 and Datadog Security Labs all corroborate trufflehog as the secret-scanner used by the Shai-Hulud worm family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/12/09/shai-hulud-2-0-guidance-for-detecting-investigating-and-defending-against-the-supply-chain-attack/ • https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/npm-supply-chain-attack/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/shai-hulud-2.0-npm-worm/ • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/shai-hulud-worm/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DevSecOps engineer running TruffleHog locally against a project they cloned and ran `npm install` in (process tree still shows node parent if they used `npx trufflehog`)
  • Pre-commit hook (husky, lefthook) that wraps TruffleHog and runs under node when the user commits
  • CI runner image that pre-bakes both Node.js and TruffleHog and the runner happens to be classified as a Windows endpoint
  • Internal red-team engagement running supply-chain simulations against developer endpoints
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("husky","lefthook","pre-commit") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--no-update","--no-verification") and InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("runner","github-actions","jenkins"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (npm/node parent → trufflehog), the package directory the install was running against, and the TruffleHog command-line arguments (Shai-Hulud variants scan `~`, `/`, or specific cred paths). Check `~/.npmrc` and `~/.bun/install/cache` for the bun_environment.js sibling. 2) Contain: isolate the host, rotate the user's npm tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS/GCP/Azure keys, SSH keys and any cloud session tokens (the worm exfils every secret type TruffleHog finds). 3) Hunt: across the tenant, query for any host that contacted bun.sh / install.bun.sh in the last 30 days, then cross-check those users' GitHub accounts for newly-created public repos named Shai-Hulud* or s1ngularity*.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FileName has "trufflehog" or ProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","sh.exe","bash.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName has "trufflehog" or ActingProcessCommandLine has "trufflehog" or TargetProcessName has "trufflehog"
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","bun","sh","bash")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

npm/node descendant accessing credential & wallet files (Shai-Hulud / Nx s1ngularity stealer) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects a child process of an npm-family runtime referencing credential files (.npmrc, .ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials), crypto-wallet artefacts (wallet.dat, keystore.json, MetaMask, Exodus) or token-keyword paths. The article describes all three named campaigns harvesting exactly these targets during install: 'scans for tokens, SSH keys, and other goodies', and Nx s1ngularity stole 'GitHub tokens, npm credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets'. Rationale: Article body lists the exact stealer targets: 'tokens, SSH keys', and for Nx s1ngularity 'GitHub tokens, npm credentials, SSH keys, and crypto wallets'. Gating on an npm-family parent restricts to install-time stealer behaviour and excludes ordinary use of these files (terminal `cat`, password manager). Semgrep and Datadog Security Labs both document the same target list across the named campaigns. Cross-checked against: • https://semgrep.dev/blog/2025/security-alert-nx-compromised-to-steal-wallets-and-credentials/ • https://securitylabs.datadoghq.com/articles/learnings-from-recent-npm-compromises/ • https://nx.dev/blog/s1ngularity-postmortem • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/malicious-nx-packages-in-s1ngularity.html
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1539
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate npm packages (e.g. npm-registry-fetch, npm itself) reading .npmrc during install to determine the configured registry
  • aws-sdk JS / @aws-sdk/credential-providers spawning helpers that walk ~/.aws/credentials at startup
  • Crypto-wallet developer working on MetaMask / Exodus SDK packages locally
  • Pre-commit secret-detection hooks (gitleaks, detect-secrets) that scan .ssh / .aws paths
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm config","npm whoami","npm publish","npm login","gitleaks","detect-secrets","@aws-sdk/credential-providers"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the offending process tree and the package responsible (resolve the npm CLI's `--prefix` or current working directory at the time of the call). Examine the package.json scripts.preinstall/postinstall fields and the package metadata on the npm registry — flag if published in the last 14 days. 2) Contain: isolate, rotate npm publish tokens, GitHub PATs, AWS keys, SSH keys and crypto wallet seed phrases (assume read). Force-revoke session cookies in browser if MetaMask / wallet paths were referenced. 3) Hunt: across the tenant for the same compromised package name in `package-lock.json`, and for outbound traffic to bun.sh, webhook.site and api.github.com/user/repos in the prior 24 hours.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any (".npmrc",".ssh\\id_rsa",".ssh/id_rsa",".aws\\credentials",".aws/credentials","wallet.dat","keystore.json","MetaMask","Exodus","Ethereum","github_token","GITHUB_TOKEN","Keychains")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("npm config","npm whoami","npm login","npm publish"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","bun")

title: npm/node descendant referencing credential and wallet files

description: Detects a child process of node, npm, npx, yarn, pnpm or bun whose command line references credential files (.npmrc, .ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials), crypto wallets (MetaMask, Exodus, wallet.dat, keystore.json) or token-keyword paths. references:

source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\bun.exe) @CommandLine:(*.npmrc* OR *.ssh\\id_rsa* OR *.ssh/id_rsa* OR *.aws\\credentials* OR *.aws/credentials* OR *wallet.dat* OR *keystore.json* OR *MetaMask* OR *Exodus* OR *github_token* OR *GITHUB_TOKEN* OR *Keychains*)

npm install descendant downloading payload from non-registry host (Bun runtime / attacker drop) AIDelivery Medium
Detects an npm-family install spawning a downloader (curl, wget, PowerShell Invoke-WebRequest/DownloadString, bitsadmin, certutil) to fetch a payload from a host that is NOT a known package registry. Article describes the canonical Shai-Hulud / Mini Shai-Hulud / generic-postinstall pattern: install hook 'downloads the real payload from an attacker server, runs it, and deletes itself'. Shai-Hulud specifically downloads the Bun runtime from bun.sh. Rationale: Article body anchors the behaviour directly: the install hook 'fingerprints the machine, downloads the real payload from an attacker server, runs it, and deletes itself'. Mini Shai-Hulud and Shai-Hulud 2.0 specifically pull the Bun runtime from bun.sh during preinstall — the SuspectBunRuntimeDrop column elevates that exact case. Allowlisting the known npm registries and Bun-detection logic both come from cross-checking Microsoft, Red Canary and Datadog write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/shai-hulud-worm/ • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2025/12/09/shai-hulud-2-0-guidance-for-detecting-investigating-and-defending-against-the-supply-chain-attack/ • https://www.sysdig.com/blog/return-of-the-shai-hulud-worm-affects-over-25-000-github-repositories
ATT&CKT1105 T1059.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Native-module packages (node-gyp, electron, puppeteer, playwright, sharp, node-sass, esbuild, @swc/core) pulling prebuilt binaries from GitHub Releases or vendor CDNs during install
  • Corporate npm proxy that re-fetches dependencies from an internal Artifactory / Nexus URL
  • Developer manually piping `curl ... | sh` while node is incidentally a parent (terminal multiplexer attribution)
  • Husky / lefthook post-install scripts that download git-hook templates from GitHub
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has_any ("electron-v","prebuild","node-pre-gyp","oven-sh/bun-electron") or InitiatingProcessParentCommandLine has_any ("node-gyp rebuild","electron-builder","playwright install","puppeteer","@swc/core-"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: extract the destination host from the command line. Compare against an allowlist of (a) corporate proxies, (b) well-known prebuilt-binary hosts (github.com/<known-vendor>/releases, *.amazonaws.com/electron-, registry.npmjs.org). Pull the offending package.json's name and version and check publish age on npm. 2) Contain: if destination is bun.sh / install.bun.sh AND the user did not knowingly opt into Bun, isolate the host and assume Shai-Hulud — rotate all developer secrets per the secret-rotation runbook. 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host across all endpoints, hunt for subsequent trufflehog execution within 10 minutes, and check GitHub for repos created by the user matching Shai-Hulud* or s1ngularity*.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npm.exe","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("node.exe","npm.cmd","npx.cmd","yarn.exe","pnpm.exe","bun.exe")
| where (FileName in~ ("curl.exe","wget.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
         or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","DownloadFile","iwr ","Start-BitsTransfer"))
| where not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","registry.npmmirror.com","npm.pkg.github.com","npm.fontawesome.com","pkg.jsr.io"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| extend SuspectBunRuntimeDrop = iff(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh","install.bun.sh","github.com/oven-sh/bun"), "yes", "no")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SuspectBunRuntimeDrop, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("node","npm","npx","yarn","pnpm","bun")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("curl","wget","powershell","pwsh","bitsadmin","certutil")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Invoke-WebRequest","DownloadString","DownloadFile","iwr ","Start-BitsTransfer")
| where not (ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("registry.npmjs.org","registry.yarnpkg.com","registry.npmmirror.com","npm.pkg.github.com","pkg.jsr.io"))
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| extend SuspectBunRuntimeDrop = iff(ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("bun.sh","install.bun.sh","oven-sh/bun"), "yes", "no")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SuspectBunRuntimeDrop, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\node.exe OR *\\Node.exe OR *\\npm.cmd OR *\\npx.cmd OR *\\yarn.exe OR *\\pnpm.exe OR *\\bun.exe) (@Image:(*\\curl.exe OR *\\wget.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe) OR @CommandLine:(*Invoke-WebRequest* OR *DownloadString* OR *DownloadFile* OR *Start-BitsTransfer*)) -@CommandLine:(*registry.npmjs.org* OR *registry.yarnpkg.com* OR *registry.npmmirror.com* OR *npm.pkg.github.com* OR *pkg.jsr.io*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(node|npm|npx|yarn|pnpm|bun)(\.exe|\.cmd)?$/i
| (ImageFileName=/(curl|wget|powershell|pwsh|bitsadmin|certutil)(\.exe)?$/i OR CommandLine=/(Invoke-WebRequest|DownloadString|DownloadFile|iwr\s|Start-BitsTransfer)/i)
| NOT regex("(registry\\.npmjs\\.org|registry\\.yarnpkg\\.com|registry\\.npmmirror\\.com|npm\\.pkg\\.github\\.com|pkg\\.jsr\\.io)", field=CommandLine)
| UserName!=/\$$/
| BunFlag := if(CommandLine=/bun\.sh|install\.bun\.sh|oven-sh\/bun/i, then="yes", else="no")
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName, BunFlag], function=count())
