Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time

| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,

OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack

The Hacker News
2026-06-11 15 use cases 4 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The Vietnam-aligned threat actor known as OceanLotus has been attributed to two distinct campaigns that targeted domestic entities and stock investors with a backdoor known as SPECTRALVIPER. The campaigns involve a prolonged cyber espionage operation aimed at a Vietnamese infrastructure and transport construction corporation between mid-2024 and February 2026, as well as a supply chain attack

Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit.exe fetching unsigned setup.exe from compromised update channel · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] MSSQL sqlservr.exe spawning interactive child process — SPECTRALVIPER transport-firm initial access · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus Hits Vietnam Investors With SPECTRALVIPER in FireAnt Attack
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] DtlCrashCatch.dll side-load — SPECTRALVIPER stage-2 loader · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 hash sightings across endpoints · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe outbound to SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement · OAuth consent / suspicious app grant
FireAnt Metakit.exe fetching unsigned setup.exe from compromised update channel AIDelivery High
Hunts the supply-chain initial-access vector described by ESET: the legitimate FireAnt Metakit stock-investor client downloading setup.exe from metakit.fireant.vn/Software/ — the update path lacks signature validation and was used to push the SPECTRALVIPER downloader between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026. Pivots on the Metakit→setup.exe parent-child pair and on file writes of setup.exe sourced from the update URL. Rationale: Anchored to the article's named update URL (metakit.fireant.vn/Software/version.xml), the legitimate client name (Metakit.exe) and the article's named dropped binary (setup.exe). The parent-child pair is the article's exact described execution path; correlation with the actual download URL keeps FP near-zero. No external corroboration searched — IOCs are from the ESET-sourced article itself.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine FireAnt Metakit auto-update after vendor remediates the channel (will still match parent-child but the URL should be clean again)
  • User manually re-running an old downloaded setup.exe from Downloads folder without the network hit
  • Endpoint testing / IR engineer detonating the article's IOC in a lab
  • Metakit re-installer launched by an admin from a known-good MSI repackage
Suppression filter
| where SHA256 !in (dynamic(["<known-good Metakit setup hashes from vendor>"]))
Response runbook
Triage: pull the SHA256 of the spawned setup.exe and compare against the article's SHA1s (865A1739..., B0FEA981..., 48FEBB91..., 511B7745..., 8CD78B8D...) and VT; check whether the download URL was metakit.fireant.vn or a typo-squat. Contain: isolate the host, block egress to metakit.fireant.vn at proxy until vendor confirms channel is clean, kill setup.exe and any child of OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe spawned afterwards. Hunt: pivot on the device for DtlCrashCatch.dll writes, OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe outbound to financemachinelearning.com / gatewayrvcenter.com, and the SPECTRALVIPER hash list across the rest of the estate.
let Window = 7d;
let UpdateChannelHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Window)
    | where RemoteUrl has "metakit.fireant.vn/Software" or RemoteUrl has "metakit.fireant.vn"
    | project NetTime = Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, UpdateUrl = RemoteUrl, RequestingProc = InitiatingProcessFileName;
let SetupSpawns = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(Window)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "Metakit.exe"
    | where FileName in~ ("setup.exe")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, AccountName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;

| where isnull(NetTime) or abs(datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, NetTime)) < 600

DtlCrashCatch.dll side-load — SPECTRALVIPER stage-2 loader AIInstallation High
Hunts the article's named side-loaded DLL. ESET reports the FireAnt SPECTRALVIPER chain uses a legitimate signed binary to load a rogue DtlCrashCatch.dll from a non-standard path; the DLL then injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. The DLL name is unique enough to alert on as a single-event signature. Rationale: DtlCrashCatch.dll is the exact rogue DLL name in the ESET writeup — high enough specificity that a name-only match is reliable. Covers both the drop (file create) and the abuse (image load) so we catch it pre- and post-injection. No external corroboration was needed since the DLL name is a unique campaign indicator from the article.
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1574.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Reverse-engineer or malware-analyst opening the sample on an EDR-protected host
  • IR team copying the IOC to a forensic share that's running EDR
  • Threat-hunting tooling distributing the hash/IOC across endpoints for sweeps
  • Backup software touching a quarantined copy of the DLL
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !startswith @"C:\Users\<known-malware-analyst>\" and DeviceName !in ("SOC-RE-01", "SOC-IR-02")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the DLL hash against the article's SHA1 list and pull the loading signed binary's path — that's the side-load host that needs to be acquired. Contain: isolate the host, kill the loading process tree, take a memory image of OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe (injection target) before reboot. Hunt: search the file hash and all five SPECTRALVIPER SHA1s across the estate, pivot on OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe outbound to the two C2 domains and the eight IOC IPs.
union
(DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "ImageLoad", FolderPath, SHA256, LoadingProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoadingProcPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, LoadingCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
    | where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileRenamed", "FileModified")
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "FileWrite", FolderPath, SHA256, LoadingProc = InitiatingProcessFileName, LoadingProcPath = InitiatingProcessFolderPath, LoadingCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where TargetFileName =~ "DtlCrashCatch.dll"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, EventType
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe outbound to SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure AICommand & Control Medium
Detects the article's SPECTRALVIPER post-injection beacon: after DtlCrashCatch.dll injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, the hollowed OneDrive process beacons to financemachinelearning[.]com (FireAnt cluster) or gatewayrvcenter[.]com (transport-corp cluster). Legitimate OneDrive Sync should never talk to either. Rationale: Both C2 domains (financemachinelearning.com, gatewayrvcenter.com) are named directly in the ESET-sourced article and the eight IPs / four additional sibling domains are the pre-extracted IOC bundle. The OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe initiating-process pivot keys directly off the article's stated injection target. Both halves trigger independently so we don't miss a beacon if the injection target evolves.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1055 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR team navigating to the IOC domains from a sandboxed analyst VM
  • Threat-intel feed enrichment service probing the IOCs from a TI host
  • Security researcher sinkholing one of the domains and querying it from the corporate net
  • User typo-resolving a similar lookalike domain (unlikely on the listed names)
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("TI-SANDBOX-01", "IR-ANALYST-VM")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the initiating process — if OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe is the initiator, treat as confirmed SPECTRALVIPER injection and skip straight to contain. Pull the PID's loaded modules for DtlCrashCatch.dll. Contain: isolate host, sinkhole the domain at corporate DNS, block the IP at the egress firewall, and rotate any credentials cached on the host. Hunt: pivot on aid/DeviceName for the FireAnt update channel (UC1) and DtlCrashCatch.dll writes (UC2); sweep the estate for the SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 hashes.
let SpectralC2Domains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com","gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let SpectralC2IPs = dynamic(["38.60.245.37","139.99.33.239","139.162.11.152","139.180.128.42","142.91.98.77","166.88.77.186","194.68.26.241","103.119.47.104"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe"
   or RemoteIP in (SpectralC2IPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (SpectralC2Domains)
| where (InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe" and (RemoteIP in (SpectralC2IPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (SpectralC2Domains)))
     or (RemoteIP in (SpectralC2IPs) or RemoteUrl has_any (SpectralC2Domains))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol
| order by Timestamp desc

union isfuzzy=true
(ImNetworkSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DstIpAddr in (SpectralC2IPs) or DstHostname in~ (SpectralC2Domains) or Url has_any (SpectralC2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, ProcOrUrl = coalesce(Url, DstHostname), DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber, Source = "Network"),
(ImDnsActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where DnsQuery in~ (SpectralC2Domains)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, ProcOrUrl = DnsQuery, DstIpAddr = DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber = 53, Source = "DNS")

SPECTRALVIPER SHA1 hash sightings across endpoints AIInstallation High
Direct IOC sweep for the five SPECTRALVIPER-related SHA1 hashes ESET published with the FireAnt / Vietnam-transport reports. Catches the binaries at file-write, image-load, or process-start time and surfaces any host where they touched disk. Rationale: Five SHA1 hashes are taken verbatim from the article's pre-extracted IOC bundle. Hash-based sweeps are the cleanest low-FP article-specific detection when an EDR vendor has published the bundle. Covers process-start, file-write, and image-load shapes so we catch the file even if the host never actually executes it.
ATT&CKT1027 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel platform syncing IOC samples to a malware vault that's running EDR
  • Reverse-engineer downloading the public sample to an EDR-protected analysis VM
  • SOAR enrichment fetching the sample via VirusTotal for triage
  • Backup software touching the malware vault
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in ("MAL-VAULT-01", "IR-SANDBOX-01", "TI-ENRICH-01")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm device isn't a known malware-analysis or IR sandbox — if not, treat as a confirmed SPECTRALVIPER hit. Pull the executing user, parent process, and the file's origin (FileOriginUrl). Contain: isolate host, capture memory + disk, hash-block the file across EDR and SMG. Hunt: pivot to UC2 (DtlCrashCatch.dll), UC3 (OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe → C2), and UC5 (MSSQL post-exploit) on the same host and on any host that talked to the same C2 IP/domain in the last 90 days.
let SpectralSHA1 = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
(DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 in~ (SpectralSHA1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="FileEvent", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 in~ (SpectralSHA1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ProcessEvent", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine = ProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceImageLoadEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d) | where SHA1 in~ (SpectralSHA1)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source="ImageLoad", FileName, FolderPath, SHA1, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| order by Timestamp desc
let SpectralSHA1 = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D","B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194","48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947","511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB","8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
    | where TargetFileSHA1 in~ (SpectralSHA1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Source="FileEvent", TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(ImProcessCreate
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d)
    | where SHA1 in~ (SpectralSHA1)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, Source="ProcessCreate", TargetFileName=TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath=TargetProcessName, TargetFileSHA1=SHA1, ActingProcessName=ParentProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine=ParentProcessCommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

MSSQL sqlservr.exe spawning interactive child process — SPECTRALVIPER transport-firm initial access AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the article's suspected initial-access path for the Vietnamese transport construction firm: exploitation of a public-facing MS SQL Server. Catches sqlservr.exe spawning shells, scripting hosts, or LOLBins — the standard tell of xp_cmdshell or post-RCE foothold installation that preceded the SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load deployment on three hosts in that network. Rationale: Anchored to the article's stated suspected initial-access vector ("exploitation of remote code execution vulnerabilities in a public-facing Microsoft SQL server") and the article's description of follow-on DLL side-loading + lateral movement. sqlservr.exe → cmd/powershell is the textbook xp_cmdshell or RCE-foothold pattern; the LOLBin set covers downloader and host-recon behaviour the article explicitly says preceded SPECTRALVIPER deployment.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • DBA running diagnostic xp_cmdshell on an internal SQL instance
  • SCCM / Tanium client invoking SQL maintenance scripts that shell out
  • SQL Agent jobs that legitimately call cmd.exe for ETL / backup
  • Vendor monitoring agent shelling out from sqlservr.exe to whoami/ipconfig
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !in~ ("NT SERVICE\\MSSQLSERVER", "NT SERVICE\\SQLSERVERAGENT") or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("DownloadString","IEX","FromBase64String","-enc ","EncodedCommand","http://","https://")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm whether the SQL host is internet-facing (lookup PublicIP + edge firewall rules); if so, treat as a probable RCE foothold. Capture sqlservr.exe error log and the spawned process command line. Contain: isolate host from the internet edge, kill the child process, snapshot disk + memory, suspend the SQL service account from interactive logon. Hunt: pivot for DtlCrashCatch.dll on the host (UC2), SPECTRALVIPER C2 (UC3), and any of the 5 SHA1s (UC4) on the same host and on three other hosts in the same network segment (ESET reports three variants across the network).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "sqlservr.exe"

title: MSSQL Server Spawning Shell/LOLBin Child (SPECTRALVIPER Suspected Initial Access)
id: 3f9a2d11-5b4c-4f6e-a3d7-c1b9d2e8f502
description: Detects sqlservr.exe spawning interactive shells or LOLBins — consistent with the public-facing MS SQL Server exploitation path ESET suspects in the OceanLotus Vietnam transport campaign.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059.001
  - attack.t1059.003
  - attack.initial_access
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\sqlservr.exe'
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\wget.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\\sqlservr.exe OR *\\SQLSERVR.EXE OR *\\Sqlservr.exe) @Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\WScript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\whoami.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^sqlservr\.exe$/i ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|curl|wget|net|net1|whoami|systeminfo|nltest|ipconfig|tasklist)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="sqlservr.exe" (Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe","nltest.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process Processes.process Processes.process_path Processes.process_hash | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where count > 0

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic

    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

references:

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```

    from datamodel=Web

    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or SHA1 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037") or MD5 in~ ("865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )
| order by Timestamp desc

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["865A1739337D3303B3AB02C5E694C22B79C42B7D", "B0FEA981D02F6F76DE81EBAEFCB68B7D205D6194", "48FEBB91A10D1462461A012FAFC0918BB028E947", "511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39FB", "8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B00037"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] FireAnt Metakit updater spawning unexpected child processes (supply-chain hunt)
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children · Article-specific behavioural hunt — OceanLotus: From external espionage to domestic targeting
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load: DtlCrashCatch.dll injecting OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe · [LLM] OceanLotus renamed SysInternals ProcDump masquerading as windbg.exe · [LLM] SPECTRALVIPER sample hash hunt across process and file telemetry · RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure (domains/IPs from 2024-2026 campaigns) · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains · DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement
OceanLotus SPECTRALVIPER C2 infrastructure (domains/IPs from 2024-2026 campaigns) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts beacons from any host to the SPECTRALVIPER C&C domains and IPs ESET tied to the FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack and the Vietnamese infrastructure-construction intrusion. High fidelity because these are dedicated APT32 infrastructure published by ESET and corroborated by Elastic Security Labs / The Hacker News. Rationale: All 6 domains and 8 IPs are listed verbatim in the ESET writeup IOC tables. Corroborated against Elastic Security Labs' original SPECTRALVIPER report and The Hacker News coverage (thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html). These are dedicated APT32 C2 — any beacon is high-fidelity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sinkhole / threat-intel research box deliberately resolving the domains for analysis
  • Internal threat-hunting / honey-call sensors
  • Security vendor sandbox detonations on managed endpoints
  • Stale shared-hosting IP reuse where 139.99.33.239 / OVH ranges legitimately host other tenants long after OceanLotus has rotated
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") and AccountName has_any ("thunt","soc","research"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pivot from RemoteIP/RemoteUrl back to InitiatingProcessFileName + InitiatingProcessCommandLine to identify the host process — is it OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe, a renamed signed binary, or a FireAnt updater child? Pull the parent chain and SHA1/SHA256 for VT lookup. Step 2 (contain): Network-isolate the device via Defender MDE 'Isolate device' action, block the resolved IP at perimeter, and preserve memory before reboot for SPECTRALVIPER's in-memory payload. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all DeviceImageLoadEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll, all DeviceProcessEvents where ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName matches procdump variants but FileName does not, and any other host that resolved the same C2 domain in the last 90 days.
let SVDomains = dynamic(["gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","financemachinelearning.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let SVIPs = dynamic(["139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (SVIPs)
   or RemoteUrl has_any (SVDomains)
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteIP, RemoteUrl, RemotePort, Protocol, ReportId
| order by Timestamp desc
let SVDomains = dynamic(["gatewayrvcenter.com","coachcybersecurity.com","mxprodesign.com","power-sync-services.com","financemachinelearning.com","leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
let SVIPs = dynamic(["139.180.128.42","139.99.33.239","166.88.77.186","103.119.47.104","139.162.11.152","142.91.98.77","38.60.245.37","194.68.26.241"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (CommonSecurityLog | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where DestinationIP in (SVIPs) or DestinationHostName has_any (SVDomains) | project TimeGenerated, DeviceVendor, SourceIP, SourceUserName, DestinationIP, DestinationHostName, DestinationPort, RequestURL),
  (DnsEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where Name has_any (SVDomains) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, ResultCode),

SPECTRALVIPER DLL side-load: DtlCrashCatch.dll injecting OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe AIInstallation High
Hunts the SPECTRALVIPER loader chain: a legitimate signed binary side-loads a rogue DtlCrashCatch.dll, which then injects into OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to execute the backdoor in a trusted process. The DLL filename is APT32-specific and the OneDrive sync-service injection target is unusual for any benign software. Rationale: `DtlCrashCatch.dll` and the OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe injection target are named explicitly in the Hacker News writeup and the Elastic Security Labs report on SPECTRALVIPER. Both are non-standard strings — DtlCrashCatch is not a Microsoft DLL and OneDrive's signed sync-service is rarely a CreateRemoteThread/injection target outside this campaign. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1055.001 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Microsoft Delivery Optimization or telemetry components that happen to share the DtlCrashCatch naming convention (verify Microsoft signature + Authenticode chain)
  • Legitimate OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe launched by OneDrive.exe in C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\Microsoft\OneDrive — the query filters parent==OneDrive.exe out
  • Endpoint research/sandbox detonation that intentionally loaded the sample
  • Memory-analysis tooling (e.g. WinDbg, x64dbg) loading a captured sample for reverse-engineering
Suppression filter
| where DLLSHA1 !in ("<microsoft-signed-hashes-if-any-emerge>") and LoaderPath !startswith @"C:\Program Files\Microsoft"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the loader binary that side-loaded DtlCrashCatch.dll — its SHA1/SHA256 and Authenticode signer. Cross-check against the ESET sample list (e.g. 41CB8CD78B8DB76563E4F972ABE817CEEE9CF9B0 et al.). Confirm DtlCrashCatch.dll is not Microsoft-signed. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the device, kill OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe and the parent loader process, preserve a memory dump (SPECTRALVIPER is in-memory), and submit DLL + loader to the malware team. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep DeviceFileEvents for DtlCrashCatch.dll writes 30 days back, look at neighbouring files dropped to the same folder (loader EXE), and pivot to DeviceNetworkEvents from OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe to surface SPECTRALVIPER C2.
let LoaderDLL = "DtlCrashCatch.dll";
let InjectTarget = "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe";
let LoadEvents = DeviceImageLoadEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ LoaderDLL or FolderPath endswith strcat(@"\", LoaderDLL)
  | project LoadTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, DeviceName, DLLPath=FolderPath, DLLSHA1=SHA1, LoaderProc=InitiatingProcessFileName, LoaderPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, LoaderCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, LoaderSHA1=InitiatingProcessSHA1, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let InjectEvents = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ InjectTarget
  | where InitiatingProcessFileName !~ "OneDrive.exe" and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !contains @"\Microsoft\OneDrive\"
  | project InjectTime=Timestamp, DeviceId, OneDriveCmd=ProcessCommandLine, OneDriveParent=InitiatingProcessFileName, OneDriveParentPath=InitiatingProcessFolderPath;
LoadEvents
| union InjectEvents
| order by LoadTime desc, InjectTime desc
let LoaderDLL = "DtlCrashCatch.dll";
let InjectTarget = "OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe";
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImFileEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetFileName =~ LoaderDLL or TargetFilePath endswith strcat(@"\", LoaderDLL) | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA1, Source="file_event"),
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where TargetProcessName =~ InjectTarget | where ParentProcessName !~ "OneDrive.exe" | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine, Source="process_create"),
  (SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d) | where EventID == 4688 | where NewProcessName endswith strcat(@"\", InjectTarget) | where ParentProcessName !endswith @"\OneDrive.exe" | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, Source="sec_4688")
| order by TimeGenerated desc

OceanLotus renamed SysInternals ProcDump masquerading as windbg.exe AIInstallation High
Hunts the SPECTRALVIPER stager pattern where OceanLotus copies/renames the legitimately signed Sysinternals ProcDump utility to windbg.exe (or other names) to load an unsigned DONUTLOADER DLL. Pivots on the mismatch between the PE OriginalFileName and the on-disk filename. Rationale: The renamed-ProcDump-as-windbg trick is described in both the ESET writeup and the prior Elastic Security Labs SPECTRALVIPER report. Anchoring on PE OriginalFileName=procdump* with FileName!=procdump* is a high-fidelity OPSEC-tell that catches the masquerade even when the attacker varies the cover name. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://www.elastic.co/security-labs/elastic-charms-spectralviper • https://attack.mitre.org/groups/G0050/
ATT&CKT1036.003 T1218 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR / DFIR analyst running a renamed ProcDump for evidence collection (e.g. dump-lsass.exe wrapper) — common in vendor playbooks
  • Sysmon/EDR-driven memory-dump automation that ships ProcDump under a campaign-specific filename
  • Veeam / backup tools repackaging ProcDump inside a vendor-named binary
  • Sysadmins copying ProcDump to a tools directory under a generic name like dump.exe
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !in~ ("ir-analyst","dfir-svc") and InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("crowdstrike-falcon.exe","defendpoint.exe")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Capture the renamed binary's SHA256 and Authenticode chain — confirm the certificate matches Microsoft Sysinternals. Inspect the command line for an unsigned DLL load hint (e.g. `-accepteula`, `-ma <pid>`, or DLL paths). Step 2 (contain): Pull the binary, the sibling DLL it side-loaded (likely DONUTLOADER), and isolate the host. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot to DeviceImageLoadEvents from this PID for unsigned DLLs loaded out of the same folder, then to DeviceNetworkEvents to surface SPECTRALVIPER beacons (overlap with UC1).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName in~ ("procdump.exe","procdump64.exe","Procdump")
| where FileName !in~ ("procdump.exe","procdump64.exe")
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName has "Sysinternals" or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has "Procdump"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessVersionInfoOriginalFileName, ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA1, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileOriginalName in~ ("procdump.exe","procdump64.exe","Procdump")
| where ActingProcessName !endswith @"\procdump.exe" and ActingProcessName !endswith @"\procdump64.exe"
| where ActingProcessFileCompany has "Sysinternals"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessFileOriginalName, ActingProcessFileCompany, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Renamed Sysinternals ProcDump (Possible OceanLotus DONUTLOADER Stager)

description: Detects ProcDump.exe / Procdump64.exe executed under a non-canonical filename (e.g. windbg.exe). OceanLotus / APT32 has been observed using a renamed ProcDump to side-load an unsigned DONUTLOADER DLL that ultimately runs SPECTRALVIPER.

SPECTRALVIPER sample hash hunt across process and file telemetry AIInstallation Medium
Sweeps endpoint telemetry for the 20 SHA1 hashes ESET attributes to SPECTRALVIPER and its loaders observed in the 2024-2026 FireAnt / construction-corp campaigns. Catches a hit even when the attacker renames the binary or hides it behind a side-load. Rationale: All 20 SHA1s are listed verbatim in the ESET IOC block. Cross-checked against the Hacker News / Cyberpress writeups which cite the same campaign. Hash-based detection is the lowest-FP control we can deploy against SPECTRALVIPER samples until they rotate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/oceanlotus-hits-vietnam-investors-with.html • https://cyberpress.org/oceanlotus-hits-stock-investors/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1027 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • AV / EDR vendor sandbox detonating a captured sample on a managed lab host
  • Threat-intel team intentionally executing the sample in a quarantined network
  • ESET's own telemetry feed re-surfacing the hash via reputation downloads
  • Legitimate sibling Sysinternals or Microsoft binary that ESET miscategorised (low probability — verify Authenticode if hit)
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): On any hit, pull the full process tree (parent + grandparent), Authenticode signing chain of every binary in that tree, and the SHA256 (the article gives SHA1 — convert at hit time). Step 2 (contain): Isolate the device, block the SHA1/SHA256 in MDE Indicators, and block the C2 list (UC1). Pull a memory image — SPECTRALVIPER lives in-memory in OneDrive.Sync.Service.exe. Step 3 (hunt): Pivot from the executing user's mailbox to look for the FireAnt Metakit installer download (March 2026 supply-chain window), and run UC2/UC3/UC4 across the same host's 90-day timeline.

FireAnt Metakit updater spawning unexpected child processes (supply-chain hunt) AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the OceanLotus FireAnt Metakit supply-chain attack (Oct 2025-Mar 2026) where the legitimate auto-updater fetched a trojanised payload from the compromised vendor update server. Detects FireAnt-branded binaries spawning script hosts, LOLBins, or unsigned executables from user-writable paths — the shape a backdoored update would produce. Rationale: FireAnt Metakit is the named compromised vendor in the ESET writeup; the supply-chain window is Oct 2025-Mar 2026. Pairing FireAnt-branded parent with LOLBin or user-writable-path unsigned child is the shape any backdoored update would produce — high signal for a Vietnam-region SOC that has any FireAnt installs on the fleet. Cross-checked against: • https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/ • https://gbhackers.com/oceanlotus-targets-stock-investors/ • https://cybersecuritynews.com/oceanlotus-apt-compromises-fireant-metakit/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059 T1218
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FireAnt itself legitimately invoking msiexec.exe for a real version-bump installer
  • Vietnamese-language localisation tools wrapped into the updater (cmd.exe with chcp 65001) running on first launch
  • User-installed FireAnt extensions / plug-ins that bundle Lua/JS scripting and shell out to wscript.exe
  • Crash-handler workflows that legitimately spawn certutil.exe to upload symbols
Suppression filter
| where not(ChildImage =~ "msiexec.exe" and ChildCmd has_any ("FireAnt.msi","Metakit.msi") and ChildSigner has "FireAnt")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Verify Authenticode signer on the FireAnt parent binary — confirm it's actually the legitimate vendor cert. Capture the child's full command line and SHA256. If the child writes a DLL with `DtlCrashCatch` in its name or drops a renamed ProcDump, escalate immediately to UC2/UC3. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, block the parent FireAnt binary by SHA256 in MDE, and rotate any trading-account credentials that may have been entered through this device. Step 3 (hunt): Identify every other host in the org with FireAnt Metakit installed (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory `SoftwareName has 'FireAnt'`), check their updater logs and DeviceFileEvents in the Oct 2025-Mar 2026 window for the same anomalous child shape, and run UC1 against all of them for C2 beacons.
let LOLBins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(90d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has "FireAnt" or InitiatingProcessFileName has "Metakit" or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has "FireAnt" or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "FireAnt"
| where FileName in~ (LOLBins)
   or (FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\") and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "Microsoft" and ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName !has "FireAnt")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath, ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ParentSHA1=InitiatingProcessSHA1, ChildImage=FolderPath, ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine, ChildSHA1=SHA1, ChildSigner=ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName
| order by Timestamp desc
let LOLBins = dynamic(["powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","msiexec.exe"]);
union isfuzzy=true
  (ImProcessCreate | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d) | where ParentProcessName has "FireAnt" or ParentProcessName has "Metakit" or ParentProcessCommandLine has "FireAnt" | where ActingProcessName has_any (LOLBins) or (ActingProcessName has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\AppData\Roaming\", @"\ProgramData\") and ActingProcessFileCompany !has "Microsoft" and ActingProcessFileCompany !has "FireAnt") | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessFileCompany, SHA1),
  (SecurityEvent | where TimeGenerated > ago(90d) | where EventID == 4688 | where ParentProcessName has "FireAnt" or ParentProcessName has "Metakit" | extend ChildName = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])) | where ChildName in (LOLBins) | project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account=SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: FireAnt Metakit Auto-Updater Spawning LOLBin (OceanLotus Supply Chain)
id: 9af7c2e1-6b3a-4e8d-bcef-7c1d9b0a5e44
status: experimental
description: Detects the legitimate FireAnt Metakit Vietnamese stock-investment platform spawning script-host or LOLBin children. Per ESET, OceanLotus compromised the FireAnt update server between Oct 2025 and Mar 2026 and used the updater to deliver SPECTRALVIPER.
references:
  - https://www.welivesecurity.com/en/eset-research/oceanlotus-external-espionage-domestic-targeting/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.g0050
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|contains:
      - 'FireAnt'
      - 'Metakit'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\curl.exe'
      - '\msiexec.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*FireAnt* OR *fireant* OR *Metakit* OR *metakit*) OR @ParentCommandLine:(*FireAnt* OR *Metakit*)) @Image:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\curl.exe OR *\\msiexec.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 (ParentBaseFileName=/fireant/i OR ParentBaseFileName=/metakit/i OR ParentImageFileName=/FireAnt/i) ImageFileName=/\\(powershell|pwsh|cmd|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|certutil|bitsadmin|curl|msiexec)\.exe$/i | groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241") or RemoteUrl has_any ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic(["139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241"]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com"]);
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DstIpAddr in (BadIPs)
   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

title: Outbound Connection to Article-Named IP / Domain
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0f
status: experimental
description: |

references:

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.

    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.dest IN ("139.162.11.152", "142.91.98.77", "139.180.128.42", "139.99.33.239", "166.88.77.186", "103.119.47.104", "38.60.245.37", "194.68.26.241")
    by All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Web
        where Web.dest IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by Web.src, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`]
| append
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
        where DNS.query IN ("financemachinelearning.com", "gatewayrvcenter.com", "coachcybersecurity.com", "mxprodesign.com", "power-sync-services.com", "leadingfilipinoteams.com")
        by DNS.src, DNS.query, DNS.answer
     | `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`]
DNS tunneling / TXT-heavy domain queries Command & Control Medium
Long subdomain labels + frequent queries to a single 2LD = DNS C2/exfil.
ATT&CKT1071.004 T1048.003
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemotePort == 53 and isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
| extend qlen = strlen(RemoteUrl)
| where qlen > 50
| extend SecondLevelDomain = extract(@"([\w-]+\.[a-zA-Z]{2,})$", 1, RemoteUrl)
| summarize qcount = count(), uniqueSubs = dcount(RemoteUrl), maxLabel = max(qlen)
    by DeviceName, SecondLevelDomain
| where qcount > 100 and uniqueSubs > 20
| order by qcount desc
// ASIM ImDnsActivity normalises Windows DNS, Sysmon EID 22, Linux dnsmasq, etc.
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where DnsQueryTypeName == "TXT"
| summarize Queries = count(), DistinctNames = dcount(DnsQuery)
            by SrcIpAddr, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| where Queries > 200    // tune to TXT-query baseline for environment
| order by Queries desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Network_Resolution.DNS
    where DNS.message_type="QUERY"
    by DNS.src, DNS.query
| `drop_dm_object_name(DNS)`
| eval qlen=len(query)
| where qlen > 50
| rex field=query "(?<second_level_domain>[\w-]+\.[\w-]+)$"
| stats sum(count) AS qcount, dc(query) AS unique_subs, max(qlen) AS max_label
    by src, second_level_domain
| where qcount > 100 AND unique_subs > 20
| sort - qcount
Remote service execution — PsExec / SMB lateral movement Actions on Objectives High
psexec / paexec / smbexec / wmic /node — service install over SMB from remote host.
ATT&CKT1021.002 T1569.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("psexec.exe","psexesvc.exe","paexec.exe","smbexec.py")
   or (FileName =~ "wmic.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has "/node:")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by Timestamp desc

SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688            // process-create (audit-policy required)
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\psexec.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\psexesvc.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\paexec.exe"
   or (NewProcessName endswith "\wmic.exe" and CommandLine has "/node:")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: PsExec / SMB Lateral Movement Tooling Execution
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d03
status: experimental
description: |

    pivots over SMB. Pair with `wmic /node:` for the full cluster.
references:

author: Clankerusecase

        Image|endswith:
            - '\psexec.exe'

            - '\psexesvc.exe'
            - '\paexec.exe'
            - '\csexec.exe'
            - '\remcom.exe'

    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process_name, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

        OR Processes.process="*-w hidden*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"

        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("D511B77459673EC42163F19E300FF1D233B6C39F", "59A8553A4F8130F576AB234E0B220BE4D4DA0E98", "9CA1A5C7F79882DB913534C1E62B26BCDCB9F6DD", ShinyHunters PeopleSoft Campaign C2/Exfil Infrastructure Match AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts for any host in the estate contacting the IP set and azurenetfiles.net domain attributed to the ShinyHunters PeopleSoft data-theft campaign that breached Nottingham University. High-fidelity IOC sweep across endpoint, DNS, and perimeter telemetry. Rationale: Uses the exact pre-extracted IOC list from the article (7 IPs and azurenetfiles.net). High-fidelity because these are campaign-specific infrastructure, not generic hosting. Cross-checked against BleepingComputer article body listing the IOCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1041 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Network_Resolution.DNS
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Threat-intel sandbox / VirusTotal infrastructure scanning the same IPs
  • Security researcher pivot lookups from analyst workstations
  • Misconfigured allowlist test traffic from network team
  • Legitimate Microsoft Azure file-share domains masquerading similar to azurenetfiles.net (verify the apex domain exactly)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("MsSense.exe","SenseIR.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpCmdRun.exe") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath !startswith "C:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows Defender"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify all hits per host, capture the initiating process and account, check if endpoint sits in PeopleSoft application/database tier. 2) Contain: block the IP set and domain at perimeter and EDR network filter, isolate any confirmed-beaconing host, rotate credentials of accounts logged on that host. 3) Hunt: pivot on initiating process hashes/paths across the fleet, search 90-day DNS for azurenetfiles.net subdomains, review PeopleSoft web tier logs for the same source IPs hitting /pls/, /psp/, /psigw/ endpoints.

Oracle PeopleSoft Gadget Chain Exploitation Detection AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for serialised Java gadget-chain payloads being POSTed to PeopleSoft URI paths (/pls/, /psp/, /psigw/, /PSIGW/, /PSEMHUB/), which the article identifies as the ShinyHunters initial-access vector. Targets the web tier where the deserialisation occurs. Rationale: Article explicitly states ShinyHunters used a 'gadget chain of zero-days and old vulnerabilities' against PeopleSoft and that exploitation depends on instance configuration. Targets the canonical PeopleSoft URI paths and the parent->child of an app-server process spawning an OS shell that always indicates RCE. Cross-checked against: • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/nottingham-university-data-breach-affects-over-450-000-students/
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate PeopleSoft integration broker (PSIGW) XML-message POSTs that exceed 30KB
  • PeopleSoft Application Engine (PSAE) batch jobs invoking cmd.exe for legitimate file operations
  • Patch deployment scripts running under the PeopleSoft service account
  • Tuxedo/Weblogic admin tooling launching cmd.exe for diagnostics
Suppression filter
| where not (csUserAgent has_any ("PSIGW-Integration","PeopleSoft-Integration","OracleProcMgr") and cIP startswith "10.")
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full POST body if WAF retained it, identify the IIS site/app, check whether the source IP is one of the campaign IOCs, capture the spawned child-process tree. 2) Contain: block the source IP at WAF/edge, isolate the PeopleSoft web tier host pending forensic image, rotate the PeopleSoft service-account credential and any cached Kerberos tickets. 3) Hunt: search 60d for the same URI + bytes_in pattern across all PeopleSoft instances including Malaysia and China campuses, dump PeopleSoft component-level access logs, validate patch level vs Oracle CPU and ShinyHunters claimed CVE chain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("psappsrv.exe","psntsrv.exe","PSAESRV.exe","tuxedo.exe","tmadmin.exe","WSL.exe","java.exe","javaw.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("PSAPPSRV","PSIGW","weblogic","-Dpeoplesoft")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","certutil.exe","bitsadmin.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","systeminfo.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let SuspiciousPayloadMarkers = dynamic(["rO0AB","aced0005","ysoserial","CommonsCollections","javassist","java.util.PriorityQueue","sun.rmi.server"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(W3CIISLog

  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, sSiteName, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csBytes, scStatus, csUserAgent),

  | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, RequestURL, RequestMethod, ReceivedBytes, DeviceVendor, Message)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
